quest.title: A-Toymaking We Shall Go
quest.description: A toy merchant from Fontaine seems to be struggling with the source materials of his products...
quest.rewards_formatted: Mora x20000, Hero's Wit x2, Mystic Enhancement Ore x4

talks.objective: Go to the Adventurers' Guild in Inazuma

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: Traveler and Paimon, you're right on cue!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Right on cue for what?

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: For a commission that's suited for you! I was just about to reach out to you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A commission that's suited for us... Don't tell Paimon that you want us to look for things or drive hilichurls off.

choices.text: Or to pick some garbage up on the rooftop...

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: Oh, don't misunderstand. The commission is indeed suited for you, and by "suited" I mean...

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: It's fun, and there are rich rewards to be had as well.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Rich rewards!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Being fun certainly doesn't seem important to Paimon, huh?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: U—Um... Being fun is also important! So, what is this commission about?

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: The requester is a toy merchant from Fontaine. His name is Bertrand. He came to sell toys in Inazuma and is currently looking for an assistant to help him with toy-making.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: He's a businessman, after all. That explains why he promised some very generous rewards when he put up the request at the Adventurers' Guild.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: But he somehow can't leave Ritou at the moment. Please go and ask him about the details of the commission.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sure, we'll head to Ritou and look for him right away!

choices.text: Or to fetch some suspicious-looking goods...

talks.objective: Go to Ritou and look for Bertrand

dialogues.speaker: Bertrand
dialogues.text: Ahahah! I now have everything ready! I'll sell each toy for thousands of Mora. Then, with tens of thousands of them sold...

dialogues.speaker: Bertrand
dialogues.text: I can easily earn tens of millions... Hahaha...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hello, are you Bertrand?

dialogues.speaker: Bertrand
dialogues.text: Ah yes, I am.

dialogues.speaker: Bertrand
dialogues.text: Are you two toy buyers who caught wind of my business?

dialogues.speaker: Bertrand
dialogues.text: But it's a shame that I can't sell you any toys yet, because I haven't started mass production.

dialogues.speaker: Bertrand
dialogues.text: But no worries, the production line is being built as of now. You can register and make a deposit if you're interested. I'll inform you when the toys are ready, and then you can proceed to pay the balance...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hold your horses! We're not here to buy your toys.

dialogues.speaker: Bertrand
dialogues.text: Oh, you aren't toy buyers... So if you've got something to say, tell me quick. Don't waste my time.

dialogues.speaker: Bertrand
dialogues.text: And be concise, my time is precious.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa... What a change of attitude!

response.speaker: Bertrand
response.text: Ah, so you're the assistants sent by the Adventurers' Guild! Welcome! You could've told me earlier!

response.speaker: Bertrand
response.text: Yes, I did put up that request. How should I address you two?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (A sudden change of attitude again...)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon is... Uh, Paimon.

response.speaker: Bertrand
response.text: Then, how about you?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: #I'm {NICKNAME}...

response.speaker: Bertrand
response.text: #{NICKNAME}? I think I've heard this name somewhere. Were you once... a wanted criminal too?

response.speaker: Bertrand
response.text: Well, I might've heard your name when the Tenryou Commission arres... Um, asked me to answer a few questions.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What on earth did you do to get yourself arrested by the Tenryou Commission?

response.speaker: Bertrand
response.text: *sigh* It was not a big deal. I just missed something when I made the last batch of toys... It really was a small mistake.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Not a big deal?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: A small mistake?

response.speaker: Bertrand
response.text: Hehe, those toys would explode if you triggered something inside them. That's all.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Explode?

response.speaker: Bertrand
response.text: Ahem, it's really no biggie. No one got hurt.

response.speaker: Bertrand
response.text: But the Doushin from the Tenryou Commission still confiscated my toys without a second thought... The way I see it, those toys could still be sold as lovely-looking bombs!

response.speaker: Bertrand
response.text: *sigh* When I first arrived, I borrowed some Mora from the International Trade Association to start my business. Who'd have thought that I would end up being confined in Ritou, not allowed to enter other areas of Inazuma...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You obviously had this coming...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hang on, since you owe the International Trade Association money, how do you plan to pay us?

response.speaker: Bertrand
response.text: You can rest assured — I haven't spent all my money, and I can clear my debt once I'm able to produce toys again and get them sold.

response.speaker: Bertrand
response.text: Then, I can give you the rich rewards as promised!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Is this really gonna work?

response.speaker: Bertrand
response.text: Have some confidence in Inazuma's toy market! My toys were very popular before people realized that they could explode... And you know what? They actually got even more popular after that.

response.speaker: Bertrand
response.text: Anyways, if my plan still fails in the end, I'll pay off my debt by giving all the toys to Kurisu.

response.speaker: Bertrand
response.text: Please lend me a hand, hehe.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But what do you want us to help you with?

response.speaker: Bertrand
response.text: Well, all my toys are produced by this machine that I built. It's called "One-of-a-Kind, Never-Failing, Engineer-Grade, Second-Generation Furnace-Powered Machine."

response.speaker: Bertrand
response.text: Speaking of my "One-of-a-Kind, Never-Failing, Engineer-Grade, Second-Generation Furnace-Powered Machine"...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What a tongue-twister...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yep, let Paimon think about it...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let's call it "The Great Machine"!

response.speaker: Bertrand
response.text: Wait a sec, this name is too short! It doesn't sound impressive at all!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sometimes the shorter it is, the easier it is to remember.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: "The Great Machine"... Hmm, Paimon thinks that it rolls off the tongue very well.

response.speaker: Bertrand
response.text: *sigh*... OK, I've indeed been told that I've bad taste in names. I'll take your word for it just this once.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Paimon's taste in names isn't exactly any better...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey!

response.speaker: Bertrand
response.text: Hahaha, anyways, my Great Machine can automatically analyze the materials added into it, and then choose the most appropriate method to assemble them.

response.speaker: Bertrand
response.text: But last time I added some strange mechanics that caused the toys to explode. So this time, I've reflected on the mistake and rebuilt the machine... Theoretically speaking, it should be fine.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Theoretically speaking...

response.speaker: Bertrand
response.text: That's why I need people to test it.

response.speaker: Bertrand
response.text: In all, the collection process involves three steps: Source Material Collection, Elemental Charge, and Core Activation.

response.speaker: Bertrand
response.text: We need to collect things like ores, fruits, and flowers as the base materials.

response.speaker: Bertrand
response.text: Next, we infuse the materials with elemental energy to allow the process to move forward. And finally, we power the materials with the energy drawn from the cores of elemental life forms.

response.speaker: Bertrand
response.text: Today, let's try the first step — Source Material Collection!

response.speaker: Bertrand
response.text: Here, take this Material Collector. Remember to directly put anything you collect into the Collector, lest it be contaminated by other elements.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Leave it to me.

response.speaker: Bertrand
response.text: Thanks. Let me adjust the device one last time. I'm counting on you to collect the materials!

response.speaker: Bertrand
response.text: Haha, that's a long story. I was once arrested by the Tenryou Commission due to a small accident...

choices.text: You put up a request at the Adventurers' Guild, didn't you?

dialogues.speaker: Bertrand
dialogues.text: Have you collected the source materials using the Collector? The source materials play a critical role in shaping the toys. Be careful with your choice, haha!

dialogues.speaker: Bertrand
dialogues.text: Heh! If that's the amount I'm getting for one of these, then I just need to sell 20,000 of them to pay off my debt!

dialogues.speaker: Bertrand
dialogues.text: As simple as that... Uh, you seem to have some questions, I presume?

choices.text: What do you plan to sell?

response.speaker: Bertrand
response.text: I plan to sell toys, but... Unfortunately, the toys are yet to be produced. Please check them out once I have them ready.

response.speaker: Bertrand
response.text: If you've nothing to say, then don't bother me. I'm currently making a batch of important products.

talks.objective: Return the Material Collector to Bertrand

dialogues.speaker: Bertrand
dialogues.text: How's it going? Have you collected any materials?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: They're all in the Collector.

dialogues.speaker: Bertrand
dialogues.text: Alright then, lemme add the materials to my One-of-a-Kind, Never-Failing...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's "The Great Machine."

dialogues.speaker: Bertrand
dialogues.text: Fine. Lemme add the materials to the Great Machine...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Bertrand connects the Collector to The Great Machine.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow! And what's next?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Will the machine go "chug chug chug" and then spill out the toys with "crackle and kaboom"?

dialogues.speaker: Bertrand
dialogues.text: Hahaha, that is totally...

dialogues.speaker: Bertrand
dialogues.text: Impossible.

dialogues.speaker: Bertrand
dialogues.text: What are you thinking? That's only the first step of the three processes. We're far from getting things done.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon gets it, so we need to complete all the processes, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Bertrand
dialogues.text: Yep, we need all three processes in order to produce the toys.

response.speaker: Bertrand
response.text: Look at you, always wanting a quick fix. It takes patience to make toys. We must infuse every process with...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: With what? Oh, Paimon gets it. It's toys we're making, after all, so we must infuse every process with real passion!

response.speaker: Bertrand
response.text: Yep, my passion for Mora!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... Although that's not what Paimon was thinking, Paimon does share the sentiment!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Hey...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, Paimon was just trying to make conversation.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Then, Bertrand, what do we do next? Should we move on to the following processes?

response.speaker: Bertrand
response.text: No worries. Since I've recently adjusted the machine, and this particular process hasn't been tested yet, I need to check if it works well with the materials.

response.speaker: Bertrand
response.text: This requires some time. Please come back later.
